name: The One That Stays
summary: A fresh hand tied bouquet with one crochet bloom tucked inside. When the fresh flowers fade, one remains.
story: This is the piece that holds both halves of what I make. Enjoy the fresh flowers for their week, then keep the crocheted bloom for as long as you like.
lifespan: Fresh stems for about a week. The crochet bloom stays.
care: Trim the stems and change the water every two days. Lift the crochet bloom out before the vase is emptied.
size: About 40cm tall, held in two hands.

name: Morning Market
summary: Whatever is brightest at the market that week, tied loosely with chamomile and greens.
story: Chosen from whatever is best at the market that week, so no two bunches are the same. Expect sunshine colours and a garden feel.
lifespan: About five to seven days in a cool room.
care: Trim 2cm off the stems, use a clean vase and change the water every two days.

name: Blush Letter
summary: Garden roses and spray roses in shades of blush, for the things that are hard to say out loud.
story: Soft colour does a lot of quiet work. This is the bouquet I'd send when the card matters more than the flowers.
lifespan: About a week. Garden roses open fully by day four.
care: Keep away from direct sun and air conditioning vents. Change the water every two days.

name: Twelve Reds
summary: Twelve long stemmed red roses, wrapped simply. The classic, done properly.
story: There's a reason this one never goes away. I keep it plain so the roses do the talking.
care: Recut the stems at an angle and keep the vase topped up. Roses drink a lot.

name: Quiet Field
summary: White chrysanthemums, lisianthus and soft greens. Calm, respectful, and right for a family in mourning.
story: For loss I keep the palette white and green, the colours of mourning in Chinese custom, and the shape gentle.
lifespan: About a week, often longer. Chrysanthemums are hardy.
care: Change the water every two days and remove leaves below the waterline.

name: Lily and Linen
summary: White oriental lilies with linen wrap. Tall, scented, and generous in a room.
story: Lilies fill a home with scent for days. They're not for every room, and the coach will tell you when to choose something else.
lifespan: Up to ten days as the buds open in turn.
care: Pinch out the orange pollen as each lily opens; it stains. Keep well away from cats.

name: Graduation Armful
summary: Sunflowers and statice in a bright, photo ready bouquet for convocation day.
story: Made to look good in every photo of the day, and sturdy enough to survive a long ceremony.
lifespan: About a week. Statice dries beautifully if you hang it upside down.
care: Give the sunflowers deep water; they are thirsty.

name: Potted Orchid
summary: A white phalaenopsis orchid in a stoneware pot. Blooms for weeks and suits an office.
story: Orchids are part of Singapore's story. This one flowers for weeks and can bloom again with care.
lifespan: Flowers for six to ten weeks.
care: Three ice cubes a week, bright indirect light, nothing more.

name: The Keeper Rose
summary: A single crocheted rose in a small glass bud vase. Small, lasting, and easy to keep on a desk.
story: One rose, worked stitch by stitch. It's the smallest thing I make and often the one people keep the longest.
lifespan: For as long as you keep it.
care: Dust with a soft brush. Keep out of strong sun so the colour stays true.

name: Sunday Tulips
summary: Five crocheted tulips in soft pastels. Welcome on any hospital ward and still there when they get home.
story: Many hospital wards don't allow fresh flowers. These tulips are welcome anywhere, and they come home with the patient.
lifespan: For as long as you keep them.
care: No water, no sun, no fuss. A gentle dust now and then.

name: Forever Graduation
summary: Crocheted sunflowers and daisies for convocation day, made to keep long after the gown is returned.
story: Fresh graduation bouquets are lovely for the photos. This one goes on the shelf next to the scroll.
lifespan: For as long as you keep it.
care: Keep out of strong sun so the yellows stay bright.

name: Little Quartet
summary: Four crocheted daisies tied with a ribbon. A small, cheerful thank you.
story: Four little daisies I make in batches, so they are quick to send. For Chinese families I make it with five.
lifespan: For as long as you keep it.
care: A gentle dust now and then.

name: Remembrance
summary: Crocheted white blooms and sage leaves. A keepsake for a family to hold on to after the wake.
story: Fresh flowers at a time of loss fade with the days. This is for a family who would like something that stays.
lifespan: For as long as you keep it.
care: Keep out of strong sun. Dust gently.
